title: Footprints in the Snow. None Out.
idea: classic fair-play snow mystery: a gardener found at a shed with only the finder's footprints in the snow; a snow-free outline, a cold lantern and dry boots break three alibis

cast.name: Kiri
cast.look: a quiet sharp boy of twelve, red scarf, short messy hair, round glasses

cast.name: Hana
cast.look: his teenage cousin, green parka, long ponytail, always says what the viewer thinks

cast.name: Inspector Dale
cast.look: police inspector, long grey coat, grey moustache, notebook

cast.name: Rosa
cast.look: the cook, white apron, brown hair under a cap, flour on her hands

cast.name: Mr. Hale
cast.look: a guest, velvet jacket, slick dark hair, neat moustache

cast.name: Ben
cast.look: the groundsman's son, wool cap, work jacket, tall and shy

scenes.title: One set of footprints
scenes.place: The garden shed at night under falling snow, one line of footprints in the snow leading to its shut door, an unlit lantern hanging beside it

lines.t: It snowed all night. One set of footprints. They only went in.
Old Tom, the gardener at Larkfield Manor, was in the shed. He would not come out again.
Rosa, the cook, found him at ten. Hers were the only footprints in the snow.
Nobody else came near that door. Nobody could have. The snow tells us so.
The snow tells us what it saw. That is not the same as what happened.
Kiri, you always say that. Fine. Who are we looking at?

scenes.title: Rosa
scenes.place: The warm manor kitchen at night, a big pot on the stove, a cook in an apron wiping her hands, a clock on the wall

lines.t: First, Rosa, the cook. She cooked dinner for the house from five o'clock.
I went to the shed at ten to bring Tom his soup. I opened the door. That is all.
Two kitchen girls say she never left the stove before eight.
So she walked to the door, and her prints go in. Simple.

scenes.title: Mr. Hale
scenes.place: The manor dining room at night, candles on a long table, a guest in a velvet jacket folding his napkin, snow at the window

lines.t: Next, Mr. Hale, a guest. He sat at the family table from eight until eleven.
Dinner, then cards. Ask anyone. I never went near the garden.
I did hear Tom singing in his shed at eight, from the terrace. He was alive and in good voice.
So whatever happened was after eight. And after eight, the snow was falling.

scenes.title: Ben
scenes.place: The groundsman's cottage porch at night, snow falling, a young man stamping his boots by a lamp

lines.t: Last, Ben, the groundsman's son. He lives at the cottage by the gate.
I came home from the village at ten, through the snow. I went straight to bed.
Three alibis, one dead end. Kiri, I do not see how this is possible.
Now watch closely. Three clues are hiding in plain view. Can you find them before Kiri does?

scenes.title: The first clue
scenes.place: A close view of the shed step in the snow, a dry dark outline of a lying shape on the boards with snow all around it

lines.t: Clue one. The shed step. Look at the snow around it.
On the step there is a dark, dry outline. Snow is everywhere, except in that shape.
Snow cannot fall where something already lies. He was on that step when the snow began.

scenes.title: The second clue
scenes.place: A close view of the lantern hanging by the shed door, its glass clear and its oil full, snow on its hook

lines.t: Clue two. The lantern by the door.
Tom lit it every evening at dusk. Half past six, like clockwork.
Tonight it is cold, and the oil is full. It was never lit.
So Tom was gone before half past six. He never sang at eight.

scenes.title: The third clue
scenes.place: A close view of a young man's boots on the cottage porch, dry and clean, a puddle-free boards, a warm lamp glowing

lines.t: Clue three. Ben's boots.
He says he walked through deep snow at ten. His boots are dry, and warm from the fire.
All right. I was home before eight, before it snowed. I was afraid you would blame me.
On my way past the garden at half past six I saw Mr. Hale come out of the shed alone.

scenes.title: The trick
scenes.place: The garden under snow in the dark, a drawing of a clock at six and a second clock at eight with snow falling, the shed and the manor lit in the distance

lines.t: So here is how it worked. Step one. Tom died before half past six, on that step.
Step two. At eight the snow began and covered every track of the one who was there.
Step three. Mr. Hale told us he heard singing at eight, so everyone thought it happened later.
Step four. At ten Rosa found him and made the only footprints left. The snow did the rest.
Mr. Hale, there was no light in that shed at eight. The lantern was cold.
He needed us to believe the snow made it impossible. It only made it quiet.

scenes.title: Why
scenes.place: The manor terrace at night, snow on the stone rail, lights from the dining room behind, Kiri looking out over the white garden

lines.t: The motive is two lines long. Tom had seen Mr. Hale burying a small box in the garden.
Mr. Hale did not want anyone to ask what was in it.
The three clues were there the whole time. A dry outline. A cold lantern. A pair of dry boots.
What do you walk past every day without really looking?
